## 7. Compiler support and behavior {#compiler}

**Compile for the exact processor and verify the emitted path.** The full analysis is now in [LLVM on CDNA: MFMA dependencies and waits](../cdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd).

### Target support and tools {#compiler-target-lookup}

Scope: CDNA 3 `gfx942` and CDNA 4 `gfx950`. The common FP16 builtin is enabled for both; the wider FP16, scaled MFMA and transpose-load interfaces require the reviewed `gfx950` features. [Default target support and builtin contracts](../cdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#compiler-target-lookup).

### Compiler takeaways {#compiler-summary}

- **MFMA spacing depends on the operand role and physical overlap.** Exact C reuse, partial C overlap and result reuse as A/B take different paths. [Shared FP16 example and conditions](../cdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#mfma-compiler-cases).
- **Memory completion is separate.** Direct-to-LDS writes need pending-write tracking before later LDS access. [Wait-counter handling](../cdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#llvm-copy-completion).
- **Hidden inline-assembly dependencies need an explicit audit.** Recognized machine instructions and visible operands define the automatic handling boundary. [Developer checks](../cdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#mfma-compiler-scope).

### Applicability and validation limits {#compiler-boundaries}

The analysis is pinned to LLVM `4e9d349ab86d`. Its wait-state thresholds are not measured GPU latency. Source and regression expectations were inspected; kernel compilation, LLVM regression execution and GPU execution were not performed. [Full revision, coverage and limits](../cdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#compiler-evidence).
